2025_073_8_b_24680_troy_school_district_.paragraph: Annual Comprehensive Financial Report of Troy School District for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, prepared by the Department of Business Services and presented to the Board of Education as agenda item 8.B. on November 18, 2025. Plante & Moran issued an unmodified audit opinion dated October 13, 2025, and reported no findings or questioned costs for federal awards. **Item** — Agenda item 8.B., 24680 Troy School District-0625-AUD-Final, Board of Education meeting of November 18, 2025: the district's Annual Comprehensive Financial Report with Supplementary Information for the year ended June 30, 2025, prepared by the Business Office.

**Audit** — Plante & Moran, appointed by the Troy Board of Education for the 2024-2025 fiscal year, issued an unmodified opinion on the governmental activities, each major fund, and the aggregate remaining information. The auditor's Government Auditing Standards report on internal control and compliance is dated October 13, 2025. No findings or questioned costs for federal awards were reported for the year ended June 30, 2025. Federal awards supplemental information was issued under separate cover. The transmittal letter, dated October 13, 2025, is signed by Dan Trudel, CPA, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, and Aurel Malutan, Director of Finance.

**Government-wide summary (in millions, per Management's Discussion and Analysis)**

| Item | 2025 | 2024 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current and other assets | $256.2 | $276.9 |
| Capital assets | 269.3 | 217.4 |
| Total assets | 525.5 | 494.3 |
| Deferred outflows | 71.1 | 101.4 |
| Total liabilities | 522.3 | 621.0 |
| Net pension liability | 211.6 | 288.9 |
| Deferred inflows | 129.0 | 91.4 |
| Net investment in capital assets | 125.1 | 106.6 |
| Restricted | 56.4 | 19.6 |
| Unrestricted | (236.2) | (242.9) |
| Total net position (deficit) | $(54.7) | $(116.7) |

Total expenses were $200.3 million and total revenue $262.3 million, producing a $62.0 million increase in net position. Detailed statements report total expenses of $200,306,434, charges for services of $5,762,303, operating grants and contributions of $76,046,945, total general revenue of $180,461,987, a change in net position of $61,964,801, and an ending deficit of $(54,739,779).

**Funds** — Combined governmental fund balance was $177.6 million, a decrease of $51.9 million. The General Fund decreased by $3.1 million to $33.7 million, stated as 17.4 percent of 2025 general operating expenditures. Special revenue fund balance moved from $10.4 million to $10.0 million, with the Food Service Fund down $0.9 million, the Community Service Fund down $66 thousand, and the Troy School District Preschool Fund up $0.4 million. Debt service fund balances rose $1.4 million. The 2023 Capital Projects Fund spent $57.9 million on voter-approved construction and ended with $127.4 million; sinking fund millage collections were $5.1 million; capital project fund balances fell $49.7 million.

**Budget** — The final General Fund amendment was adopted in June 2025. Budgeted revenue was increased by $3.3 million, primarily state and federal sources, including roughly $5.0 million of Section 147a(4) MPSERS Reduced UAAL revenue. Actual General Fund revenue was $190,573,261 against a final budget of $194,857,883; actual expenditures were $193,633,993 against $198,648,733.

**Capital assets and debt** — Total capital assets were $502,829,646 less accumulated depreciation and amortization of $233,540,622, for $269,289,024 net. Additions were $63.1 million. General obligation bonds outstanding totaled $230,080,000 plus $21,275,050 of unamortized premium. Standard & Poor's affirmed an AA/Stable rating in January 2025. Remaining construction commitments were $32,677,915.

**MPSERS** — Net pension liability was $211,642,114 and the net OPEB asset $36,619,750, both measured as of September 30, 2024 at a 6.00 percent discount rate. Pension contributions for the year were $38,371,759 and OPEB contributions $3,410,390.

**Context** — Spring 2025 enrollment was 12,393; the 2025-2026 budget assumes 12,074 students and a $442 per pupil foundation allowance increase. The November 8, 2022 voter-approved bond totals $555 million.
2025_073_8_b_24680_troy_school_district_.verbose:
Troy School District's Annual Comprehensive Financial Report with Supplementary Information for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025 came to the Board of Education as agenda item 8.B. at the November 18, 2025 meeting. The report was prepared by the district's Department of Business Services. The transmittal letter, dated October 13, 2025 and addressed to the Citizens of Troy and Board Members of Troy School District, is signed by Dan Trudel, CPA, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, and Aurel Malutan, Director of Finance. District offices are at 4400 Livernois Rd, Troy, Michigan 48098 (phone 248.823.4022, fax 248.823.4013, dtrudel@troy.k12.mi.us).

AUDIT AND AWARDS. The accounting firm of Plante & Moran was appointed by the Troy Board of Education to audit the 2024-2025 fiscal year and issued an unmodified opinion on the governmental activities, each major fund, and the aggregate remaining information as of June 30, 2025. A separate report on internal control over financial reporting and compliance under Government Auditing Standards is dated October 13, 2025. There were no findings or questioned costs for federal awards for the year ended June 30, 2025; federal awards supplemental information was issued under separate cover. ASBO International has awarded the district a Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for fiscal years ended June 30, 1989 through 2024; the certificate for the year ended June 30, 2024 is signed by Ryan S. Stechschulte, President, and James M. Rowan, CAE, SFO, CEO/Executive Director.

OFFICIALS. Board of Education: Dr. Nancy Philippart, President; Vital Anne, Vice President; Emina Alic, Esq., Secretary; and Trustees Ayesha Potts, Dr. Audra Melton, Matt Haupt, Esq., and Stephanie Zendler. Administration: Richard Machesky, Ed.D., Superintendent; Dan Trudel, CPA, Assistant Superintendent Business Services; Christine DiPilato, Assistant Superintendent Secondary Instruction; Kristine Griffor, Assistant Superintendent Elementary Instruction; and John Pagel, Assistant Superintendent Employee Services.

DISTRICT PROFILE. The district enrolls more than 12,000 students in twelve elementary schools, four middle schools, two traditional and one non-traditional high school, and one International Academy. Troy covers just over 26.61 square miles, is the largest city in Oakland County and the 13th largest in Michigan, with a population of approximately 80,000, over 6,000 businesses with a market value over $12 billion, and more than 57 percent of residents holding a bachelor's degree or higher. Fourteen schools have received the National Blue Ribbon Award (Barnard, Bemis, Hamilton, Leonard, Martell, Schroeder, Troy Union, Wass, Wattles, Larson, Boulan Park, Athens, Troy High, and the International Academy). Athens High School, Troy High, and the International Academy were named among the top five percent of U.S. high schools by U.S. News and World Report; Athens and Troy High report graduation rates over 99 percent. Board recognitions listed include the Michigan Association of School Boards Visionary Leadership Award, ArtServe of Michigan School Board of the Year, a top-ten tech-savvy board designation from the Center for Digital Education, and the 2023/2024 MASB Standard of Excellence Award. The building inventory totals 448.74 acres and 2,185,181 square feet serving 12,393 students, with 128.30 acres of vacant property; entries include Athens High School (398,426 square feet, 1974, 1,457 students), Troy High School (343,207 square feet, 1992, 2,023), Troy College and Career High School (37,520 square feet, 200), Baker, Boulan, Larson and Smith middle schools, International Academy East (81,455 square feet, 541), the Preschool for Early 5's and ECP (72,000 square feet, 2019, 242), the Troy Center for Transitions (61), the Administration and Services buildings, the Transportation Building, and the Rankin warehouse.

ECONOMIC OUTLOOK. Enrollment as of Spring 2025 was 12,393; the 2025-2026 budget adopted in June 2025 estimates a September 2025 count of 12,074, with approximately 66.5 percent of total General Fund revenue coming from the foundation allowance and state sources. Legislation for 2025-2026 includes a foundation allowance increase of $442 per pupil, offset by reductions in other categorical funding. On November 8, 2022 voters approved a $555 million bond to be issued in three series over 6 years with projects planned for 10 to 12 years; the first series was issued in March 2023, and the district anticipates exhausting the 2013 voter-approved bond funds in the next fiscal year.

GOVERNMENT-WIDE STATEMENTS. The MD&A summary (in millions) shows current and other assets of $256.2 (2024: $276.9), capital assets of $269.3 (217.4), total assets of $525.5 (494.3), deferred outflows of $71.1 (101.4), current liabilities of $43.5 (44.3), noncurrent liabilities of $267.2 (287.8), net pension liability of $211.6 (288.9), total liabilities of $522.3 (621.0), deferred inflows of $129.0 (91.4), net investment in capital assets of $125.1 (106.6), restricted of $56.4 (19.6), unrestricted of $(236.2) ((242.9)), and total net position (deficit) of $(54.7) million ($(116.7) million). Revenue comprised charges for services $5.8 (5.9), operating grants $76.0 (79.5), taxes $80.3 (75.9), unrestricted state aid $85.7 (89.5), and other $14.5 (17.1), totaling $262.3 (267.9). Expenses were instruction $107.6 (121.9), support services $67.1 (73.1), athletics $2.5 (2.5), food services $6.6 (6.1), community services $4.6 (4.7), and debt service $11.9 (13.8), totaling $200.3 (222.1), for a change in net position of $62.0 million (45.8).

The statement of net position reports cash and cash equivalents of $35,753,639, other receivables of $643,482, due from other governments of $24,946,712, inventory of $92,650, prepaid expenses of $264,778, restricted assets of $157,861,718, a net OPEB asset of $36,619,750, capital assets not being depreciated of $27,834,675 and depreciated capital assets net of $241,454,349, for total assets of $525,471,753. Deferred outflows total $71,112,962 (bond refunding charges $103,572, deferred pension costs $61,376,530, deferred OPEB costs $9,632,860). Liabilities total $522,347,330, including accounts payable $14,216,196, due to other governmental units $3,112,959, accrued salaries and wages $11,489,101, accrued payroll taxes and fringe benefits $6,600,256, accrued interest payable $1,646,900, unearned revenue $6,502,348, noncurrent liabilities due within one year $26,115,832 and due in more than one year $241,021,624, and net pension liability $211,642,114. Deferred inflows total $128,977,164. Net position components are net investment in capital assets $125,135,054; restricted for capital projects $14,727,662, food service $2,683,104, debt service $2,331,826, and net OPEB asset $36,619,750; and unrestricted $(236,237,175), for a total deficit of $(54,739,779).

The statement of activities reports expenses of instruction $107,575,936, support services $67,108,862, athletics $2,463,706, food services $6,554,386, community services $4,643,839, interest $11,956,905, and other debt costs $2,800, totaling $200,306,434, against charges for services of $5,762,303 and operating grants and contributions of $76,046,945, for net expense of $(118,497,186). General revenue includes property taxes levied for general purposes $42,989,827, for debt service $32,282,916, and for capital projects $5,053,012; unrestricted state aid $85,745,593; unrestricted federal grants $87,600; interest and investment earnings $9,242,345; student activities $3,837,861; and other $1,222,833, totaling $180,461,987. Change in net position was $61,964,801 from a beginning deficit of $(116,704,580).

GOVERNMENTAL FUNDS. The balance sheet reports total assets of $238,891,005 (General Fund $62,366,758; 2023 Capital Projects Fund $151,998,059; nonmajor funds $24,526,188), total liabilities of $61,248,886, and total fund balances of $177,642,119 (General Fund $33,713,795; 2023 Capital Projects Fund $127,362,799; nonmajor $16,565,525). Components include restricted debt service $3,978,726, food service $2,590,197, capital projects $129,278,099; committed community service $4,718,641 and student activities $2,597,629; assigned subsequent year's budget $3,739,629 and capital maintenance $672,125; and unassigned $29,709,645. Revenue totaled $256,561,021 (local $100,391,097, state $134,479,405, federal $8,650,528, interdistrict $13,039,991) and expenditures $308,412,478 (instruction $127,248,872, support services $70,116,421, athletics $2,664,534, food services $6,457,869, community services $5,243,340, capital outlay $63,730,932, principal $22,193,128, interest $10,754,582, other debt costs $2,800), for a net change of $(51,851,457) from a beginning balance of $229,493,576. Custodial funds held $141,161 of cash, liabilities of $40,741, and ending net position of $100,420 after additions of $247,637 and deductions of $238,141.

BUDGET COMPARISON. General Fund actual revenue of $190,573,261 came in $(4,284,622) under the final budget of $194,857,883 (original $191,544,523), and actual expenditures of $193,633,993 were $(5,014,740) under the final budget of $198,648,733. Actual instruction was $124,862,336, support services $65,245,045, athletics $2,689,271, and community services $200,311. Ending fund balance was $33,713,795 against a final budgeted $32,979,691.

CAPITAL ASSETS AND DEBT. Capital assets comprise land $1,861,010, construction in progress $25,973,665, buildings and improvements $404,736,902, furniture and equipment $69,200,671, lease asset - building $530,288, and lease assets - equipment $527,110, totaling $502,829,646, less accumulated depreciation and amortization of $233,540,622, for $269,289,024 net (2024: $217,410,385 on a $439,700,922 gross). Depreciation and amortization of $11,250,085 was charged to instruction $5,457,907, support services $5,470,874, community services $105,894, food services $112,863, and athletics $102,547. Construction commitments remaining were $31,947,589 in the 2023 Capital Projects Fund and $730,326 in the Sinking Fund, totaling $32,677,915. General obligation bonds outstanding were $230,080,000 with unamortized premium of $21,275,050. Issues outstanding include the $31,930,000 2015 refunding qualified bond (5.00 percent, maturing May 1, 2026, $3,210,000 outstanding), the $40,000,000 2016 qualified bond (2.94-4.50 percent, May 1, 2032, $27,500,000), the $7,125,000 2018 unqualified bond (3.00-3.75 percent, May 1, 2040, $5,770,000), the $22,630,000 2019 qualified bond (5.00 percent, May 1, 2034, $16,475,000), the $6,100,000 2020 unqualified bond (2.00 percent, May 1, 2035, $4,260,000), the $33,315,000 2021 refunding qualified bond (0.50-1.56 percent, May 1, 2028, $18,990,000), and the $171,370,000 2023 qualified bond (2.75-5.00 percent, May 1, 2052, $153,875,000). Debt service to maturity totals $230,080,000 of principal and $138,892,383 of interest, or $368,972,383. Lease obligations for the Troy Career Center building and equipment total $463,666 of principal and $33,930 of interest. Other long-term items include compensated absences of $8,156,977, other termination benefits of $172,500 (individual benefits range from $7,500 to $35,000), and an arbitrage liability of $6,989,263. Standard & Poor's affirmed an AA/Stable rating in January 2025.

DEPOSITS AND INVESTMENTS. The district designated nine financial institutions and used three. Bank deposits of $42,256,631 were uninsured and uncollateralized at year end. Investments subject to interest rate risk totaled $89,839,250. Credit quality holdings were Michigan Liquid Asset Fund Cash Management Money Market Fund $13,940,105 (AAm S&P), MILAF MAX Class Money Market $9,379,138 (AAm S&P), TERM - Michigan Term Series $39,895,000 (AAAf Fitch), commercial paper $10,767,981 (A1 S&P), and U.S. agency bonds and notes $79,071,269 (AA+ S&P), totaling $153,053,493. Restricted assets consist of unspent bond proceeds and related interest $152,736,952, unspent sinking fund taxes $1,203,857, and unspent debt service taxes $3,920,909.

MPSERS. Pension contribution rates ranged from 13.90 to 23.03 percent for October 1, 2023 through September 30, 2024 and 20.96 to 30.11 percent for October 1, 2024 through September 30, 2025; OPEB rates were 7.06 to 8.31 percent and 0.00 to 1.25 percent for the same periods. Required and actual pension contributions were $38,371,759, including $9,297,729 of state UAAL stabilization revenue and a one-time $2,113,411 payment referred to as 147c(2); OPEB contributions were $3,410,390. The net pension liability of $211,642,114 and net OPEB asset of $36,619,750 were measured as of September 30, 2024 from a September 30, 2023 valuation rolled forward; proportions were approximately 0.86 percent (pension) and 0.85 percent (OPEB). Pension expense was $15,138,956 and an OPEB recovery of $13,191,754 was recognized. Payables to the pension and OPEB plans were $7,746,814 and $188,318. Actuarial assumptions include entry age normal cost method, a 6.00 percent investment return and discount rate, salary increases of 2.75 to 11.55 percent, health care cost trend of 6.50 to 7.25 percent graded to 3.5 percent in year 15, PubT-2010 mortality tables with MP-2021 projection, and 3.00 percent cost of living adjustments. Statutorily required pension contributions were $37,490,675 on covered payroll of $92,923,328 (40.35 percent); OPEB contributions were $2,766,792 (2.98 percent).

STATISTICAL SECTION. Tax year 2024 taxable value was $6,606,966,343 (residential $4,422,115,610, commercial $1,372,140,290, industrial $445,619,610, personal property $367,090,833) at a 27.7900 mill rate, with estimated actual value of $13,213,932,686. The 2024 direct millages were 2.7294 homestead operating, 18.0000 non-homestead, 6.1000 debt, and 0.9606 sinking fund. The FY2025 levy of $80,953,671 produced current collections of $78,491,305 (96.96 percent) plus delinquent collections of $2,460,842, for 100.00 percent of levy collected. Principal taxpayers were led by Somerset Collections at $67,116,100 (1.02 percent), DTE Electric Co. $51,339,510, and Lithia Real Estate Inc $46,054,000; the top ten totaled $353,111,070, or 5.52 percent. Net general bonded debt was $247,376,324, 3.74 percent of taxable value and $2,773 per capita on a population of 89,209. Overlapping debt shares were City of Troy $9,082,792, Oakland County $8,214,742, and Oakland ISD $2,446,556, with direct district debt of $226,101,274 and total direct and overlapping debt of $245,845,364. The legal debt limit was $991,044,951 with net debt subject to limit of $6,051,274 (0.61 percent) and a legal debt margin of $984,993,677. Full-time equivalent employees totaled 1,072 (instruction 869, support services 178, community service 21, athletics 3, food service 1). Operating indicators for 2025 show enrollment of 12,393, operating expenditures of $193,633,993, cost per pupil of $15,624, operating revenue of $190,573,261, revenue per pupil of $15,377, 869 teaching staff, 14.32 percent of students qualifying for free or reduced meals, and an average teacher salary of $83,536. Principal employers were Corewell Health Beaumont Troy Hospital (3,260) and Troy School District (1,302). Tax abatements under PA 198 of 1974 and brownfield redevelopment agreements reduced property tax revenue by $471,000, with approximately $338,000 reimbursed by the State of Michigan. GASB Statements No. 103 and No. 104 take effect for the year ending June 30, 2026.
